draft.title: Prefixes, suffixes and base words
card: the main word that other parts can be added to. In unhappy, the base word is happy.
a word part added before a base word. It changes the meaning. Un added to happy makes unhappy, which means not happy.
a word part added after a base word. It can change the meaning or the word class. Ness added to happy makes happiness, a noun.
A base word can have both. In unkindness, un is the prefix, kind is the base word and ness is the suffix.
draft.remember: A prefix comes before a base word and a suffix comes after it. Both can change meaning.

a.q: In the word replay, which part is the prefix?
a.why: A prefix goes before the base word. Play is the base word, and re comes before it. Play is tempting, but it is the base word, not an added part.
a.clue: Which part comes before the base word?

b.q: Ayla adds the suffix ful to the base word care to make careful. What does the suffix do here?
opts: Changes the word from a noun to an adjective
Changes the word to mean the opposite
Changes the word from an adjective to a verb
Changes the word to mean it happened in the past
b.why: Care is a noun here, and careful describes someone, so it is an adjective. A suffix can change word class. Opposite meanings come from prefixes such as un, not from ful.
b.clue: Think about how careful is used in a sentence.

b.best: Changes the word from a noun to an adjective
